He called upon the Most High Ruler when enemies pressed him on every side, and the great Lord answered him with hailstones of mighty power.
He hurled war down upon a nation and destroyed those who resisted on the descent, so that the nations might know his full armament, because his war was before the Lord.
For he followed the Ruler, and in Moses’ days he showed mercy, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh, by standing against the assembly, restraining the people from sin, and stilling wicked grumbling.
They alone, being two, were preserved from six hundred thousand foot soldiers, to bring them into an inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey.
The Lord gave Caleb strength, and it remained with him until old age, so that he might mount the high places of the land; his offspring possessed an inheritance,
so that all the sons of Israel might see that it is good to walk after the Lord.
The judges too, each by his own name, whose hearts did not prostitute themselves and who did not turn away from the Lord—may their remembrance be among blessings!
May their bones flourish again from their place, and may their name pass onward to their honored sons.
Beloved by his Lord, Samuel, the Lord’s prophet, established a kingdom and anointed rulers over His people.
By the Lord’s law he judged the assembly, and the Lord visited Jacob.
By his faithfulness he was proved a prophet, and through his words he was known to be trustworthy in vision.
He called upon the Lord, the Ruler, when his enemies pressed him on every side, with an offering of a suckling lamb.
The Lord thundered from heaven and made His voice heard with a great sound.
He destroyed the leaders of the Tyrians and all the rulers of the Philistines.

Before the time of his everlasting sleep, he testified before the Lord and His anointed: “I have taken no property—not even sandals—from any human being.” And no person brought an accusation against him.
Even after he fell asleep, he prophesied and showed the king his end. He raised his voice from the earth in prophecy to wipe out the people’s lawlessness.
After him Nathan arose to prophesy in David’s days.
As fat is set apart from a peace offering, so David was set apart from the sons of Israel.
He played with lions as with young goats, and with bears as with lambs of the flock.
In his youth did he not kill a giant and remove reproach from the people, when he raised his hand with a sling stone and brought down Goliath’s pride?
For he called upon the Lord Most High, and He put strength in his right hand to remove a mighty warrior and raise the horn of His people.
Thus they glorified him with tens of thousands and praised him with blessings of the Lord when a crown of glory was brought to him.
For he destroyed enemies all around and reduced his Philistine adversaries to nothing; he shattered their horn to this day.
In every deed he gave thanks to the Holy Most High with a word of glory. With his whole heart he sang hymns and loved the One who made him.
He stationed psalm singers before the altar, to sweeten the melodies with their sound.
He gave festivals splendor and adorned the appointed seasons to their completion, while they praised His holy name and made the sanctuary resound from early morning.
The Lord took away his sins, raised his horn for ever, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.
After him arose a knowledgeable son, who because of him rested in spacious prosperity.
Solomon reigned in days of peace; God gave him rest all around, so that he might establish a house for His name and prepare a sanctuary for ever.
How wise you became in your youth! You were filled with understanding like a river.
Your soul covered the earth, and you filled it with comparisons containing riddles.
Your name reached distant islands, and you were loved for your peace.
Countries marveled at you for songs, proverbs, comparisons, and interpretations.
In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin and multiplied silver like lead.
You bent your loins toward women and were brought under power in your body.
You put a blemish upon your glory and profaned your offspring, bringing wrath upon your children and anguish because of your folly,
so that the dominion became divided and a disobedient kingdom began from Ephraim.

But the Lord will never abandon His mercy or let any of His words fail. He will never wipe out His chosen one’s descendants or remove the offspring of the one who loved Him. He gave Jacob a remnant, and David a root from him.
Solomon rested with his fathers and left after him, from his offspring, the people’s foolishness: Rehoboam, deficient in understanding, who made the people revolt through his counsel.
There was also Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin and gave Ephraim a path of sin. Their sins multiplied exceedingly, so that they were removed from their land.
They sought out every kind of wickedness, until vengeance came upon them.
Then Elijah arose, a prophet like fire, and his word burned like a torch.
He brought famine upon them and made them few through his zeal.
By the Lord’s word he held back heaven; in the same way he brought down fire three times.
How glorious you became, Elijah, through your wonders! Who can boast of being like you?
You raised a dead man from death and from Hades by the word of the Most High.
You brought kings down to destruction and glorious men from their bed.
You heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of vengeance at Horeb.
You anointed kings for retribution, and prophets as successors after him.
You were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with fiery horses.
You were recorded in rebukes for appointed times: to still anger before wrath, to turn a father’s heart toward a son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed are those who saw you and those who have fallen asleep in love; for we too will surely live.
Elijah was covered by a whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit. In his days he was not shaken by a ruler, and no one overpowered him.
No word surpassed him, and even in sleep his body prophesied.
In his life he performed portents, and at his end his works were wondrous.
Through all these things the people did not repent or turn away from their sins, until they were plundered from their land and scattered throughout all the earth.
The people were left few in number, with a ruler in David’s house. Some of them did what was pleasing, but others multiplied sins.

In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh, and he departed. He raised his hand against Zion and boasted greatly in his arrogance.
Then their hearts and hands were shaken, and they suffered pangs like women giving birth.
They called upon the merciful Lord, spreading their hands toward Him. The Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and redeemed them by Isaiah’s hand.
He struck the Assyrians’ camp, and His angel destroyed them.
For Hezekiah did what was pleasing to the Lord and stood strong in the ways of his father David, which Isaiah the prophet commanded, great and faithful in his vision.
In his days the sun went backward, and He added life to the king.
With a great spirit he saw the last things and comforted those mourning in Zion.
He showed what would happen to the end of the age, and hidden things before they came to pass.
The remembrance of Josiah is like a blend of incense prepared by a perfumer’s skill. In every mouth it will be sweet as honey, and like music at a wine banquet.
He was rightly directed in bringing the people back, and he removed the abominations of lawlessness.
He directed his heart toward the Lord; in days of lawless people he strengthened godliness.
Except for David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, they all committed offenses. For they abandoned the law of the Most High; the kings of Judah came to an end.
For they gave their horn to others and their glory to a foreign nation.
They burned the chosen city of the sanctuary and made its streets desolate,

Ezekiel saw a vision of glory, which He showed him upon a chariot of cherubim.
For He remembered the enemies in a rainstorm, and remembered to do good to those who make their ways straight.
May the bones of the twelve prophets flourish again from their place! For they comforted Jacob and redeemed them with the faithfulness of hope.
How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He too was like a seal upon the right hand.
So was Joshua son of Jozadak. In their days they built a house and raised up a holy sanctuary for the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.
Great also is the remembrance of Nehemiah, who raised our fallen walls, set up gates and bars, and rebuilt our home sites.
No one was created on earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth.
Nor was a man born like Joseph, a leader of his brothers, a support for the people; and his bones were cared for.
Shem and Seth were glorified among people, and Adam above every living creature in creation.
Simon son of Onias, the high priest, repaired the house in his lifetime and strengthened the sanctuary in his days.
By him the height of the double wall was founded, a high retaining wall around the sacred precinct.
In his days a water reservoir was hewn out, a cistern whose circumference was like a sea.
He cared for his people against a fall and strengthened the city against a siege.
How glorious he was with the people surrounding him, when he came out from the house of the veil!
He was like the morning star among clouds, like the full moon in its days,
like the sun shining upon the sanctuary of the Most High, and like the rainbow gleaming in clouds of glory,
like a rose blossom in the days of new growth, like lilies beside an outflow of water, like a shoot of Lebanon in summer days,
like fire and frankincense upon a firepan, like a vessel of beaten gold adorned with every costly stone,
like an olive tree flourishing with fruit, and like a cypress rising into the clouds.
When he took up the robe of glory and clothed himself with the fullness of splendor, as he ascended the holy altar he glorified the sanctuary’s enclosure.

When he received portions from the priests’ hands, standing himself beside the altar hearth, a crown of brothers surrounded him, like a growth of cedars in Lebanon; they encircled him like palm trunks,
all the sons of Aaron in their glory, with the Lord’s offering in their hands before the whole assembly of Israel.
As he completed his ministry at the altars, adorning the offering of the Most High Almighty,

Then the sons of Aaron cried out and sounded their hammered trumpets. They made a great sound heard as a remembrance before the Most High.
Then all the people together hurried and fell facedown upon the earth to worship their Lord, the Almighty God Most High.
The psalm singers praised with their voices; amid a very great sound the melody grew sweet.
The people entreated the Lord Most High in prayer before the Merciful One, until the Lord’s ceremony was completed and they finished His service.
Then he came down and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, to give the Lord’s blessing from his lips and to glory in His name.
They bowed down a second time to receive the blessing from the Most High.
And now bless the God of all, who does great things everywhere, who exalts our days from the womb and deals with us according to His mercy.
May He give us gladness of heart, and may there be peace in Israel in our days, throughout the days of eternity.
May He entrust His mercy to us, and in our days may He redeem us.

I remembered Thy mercy, Lord, and Thy work from of old: Thou rescuest those who wait for Thee and savest them from the hand of enemies.
I lifted my supplication from the earth and pleaded for deliverance from death.

I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, not to abandon me in days of affliction, in a time of arrogance when there was no help. I will praise Thy name continually and sing hymns with thanksgiving.
My petition was heard, for Thou didst save me from destruction and rescue me from an evil time.
Therefore I will give thanks to Thee and praise Thee and bless the Lord’s name.

Before the sanctuary I asked for her, and until the end I will seek her out.

I made progress in her; I will give glory to the One who gives me wisdom.

My inward parts were stirred to seek her out; therefore I acquired a good possession.
The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward, and with it I will praise Him.
Draw near to me, you who are uninstructed, and lodge in a house of instruction.
Why do you say you are lacking in these things, while your souls thirst exceedingly?
I opened my mouth and said, “Acquire for yourselves without silver.
“Put your neck beneath the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction. She is near at hand to be found.
“See with your own eyes that I labored a little and found much rest for myself.
“Take part in instruction at the cost of much silver, and acquire much gold through her.
“May your soul rejoice in His mercy, and may you not be ashamed in His praise.
“Do your work before the appointed time, and He will give you your reward in His time.”

For he followed the Ruler, and in Moses’ days he showed mercy, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh, by standing against the assembly, restraining the people from sin, and stilling wicked grumbling.

The Lord gave Caleb strength, and it remained with him until old age, so that he might mount the high places of the land; his offspring possessed an inheritance,
so that all the sons of Israel might see that it is good to walk after the Lord.
The judges too, each by his own name, whose hearts did not prostitute themselves and who did not turn away from the Lord—may their remembrance be among blessings!
May their bones flourish again from their place, and may their name pass onward to their honored sons.
Beloved by his Lord, Samuel, the Lord’s prophet, established a kingdom and anointed rulers over His people.
By the Lord’s law he judged the assembly, and the Lord visited Jacob.
By his faithfulness he was proved a prophet, and through his words he was known to be trustworthy in vision.
He called upon the Lord, the Ruler, when his enemies pressed him on every side, with an offering of a suckling lamb.
The Lord thundered from heaven and made His voice heard with a great sound.
He destroyed the leaders of the Tyrians and all the rulers of the Philistines.

Before the time of his everlasting sleep, he testified before the Lord and His anointed: “I have taken no property—not even sandals—from any human being.” And no person brought an accusation against him.
Even after he fell asleep, he prophesied and showed the king his end. He raised his voice from the earth in prophecy to wipe out the people’s lawlessness.
After him Nathan arose to prophesy in David’s days.
As fat is set apart from a peace offering, so David was set apart from the sons of Israel.
He played with lions as with young goats, and with bears as with lambs of the flock.
In his youth did he not kill a giant and remove reproach from the people, when he raised his hand with a sling stone and brought down Goliath’s pride?
For he called upon the Lord Most High, and He put strength in his right hand to remove a mighty warrior and raise the horn of His people.
Thus they glorified him with tens of thousands and praised him with blessings of the Lord when a crown of glory was brought to him.
For he destroyed enemies all around and reduced his Philistine adversaries to nothing; he shattered their horn to this day.
In every deed he gave thanks to the Holy Most High with a word of glory. With his whole heart he sang hymns and loved the One who made him.
He stationed psalm singers before the altar, to sweeten the melodies with their sound.
He gave festivals splendor and adorned the appointed seasons to their completion, while they praised His holy name and made the sanctuary resound from early morning.
The Lord took away his sins, raised his horn for ever, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.
After him arose a knowledgeable son, who because of him rested in spacious prosperity.
Solomon reigned in days of peace; God gave him rest all around, so that he might establish a house for His name and prepare a sanctuary for ever.
How wise you became in your youth! You were filled with understanding like a river.
Your soul covered the earth, and you filled it with comparisons containing riddles.
Your name reached distant islands, and you were loved for your peace.
Countries marveled at you for songs, proverbs, comparisons, and interpretations.
In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin and multiplied silver like lead.
You bent your loins toward women and were brought under power in your body.
You put a blemish upon your glory and profaned your offspring, bringing wrath upon your children and anguish because of your folly,
so that the dominion became divided and a disobedient kingdom began from Ephraim.

But the Lord will never abandon His mercy or let any of His words fail. He will never wipe out His chosen one’s descendants or remove the offspring of the one who loved Him. He gave Jacob a remnant, and David a root from him.
Solomon rested with his fathers and left after him, from his offspring, the people’s foolishness: Rehoboam, deficient in understanding, who made the people revolt through his counsel.
There was also Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin and gave Ephraim a path of sin. Their sins multiplied exceedingly, so that they were removed from their land.
They sought out every kind of wickedness, until vengeance came upon them.
Then Elijah arose, a prophet like fire, and his word burned like a torch.
He brought famine upon them and made them few through his zeal.
By the Lord’s word he held back heaven; in the same way he brought down fire three times.
How glorious you became, Elijah, through your wonders! Who can boast of being like you?
You raised a dead man from death and from Hades by the word of the Most High.
You brought kings down to destruction and glorious men from their bed.
You heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of vengeance at Horeb.
You anointed kings for retribution, and prophets as successors after him.
You were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with fiery horses.
You were recorded in rebukes for appointed times: to still anger before wrath, to turn a father’s heart toward a son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed are those who saw you and those who have fallen asleep in love; for we too will surely live.
Elijah was covered by a whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit. In his days he was not shaken by a ruler, and no one overpowered him.
No word surpassed him, and even in sleep his body prophesied.
In his life he performed portents, and at his end his works were wondrous.
Through all these things the people did not repent or turn away from their sins, until they were plundered from their land and scattered throughout all the earth.
The people were left few in number, with a ruler in David’s house. Some of them did what was pleasing, but others multiplied sins.
Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into its midst. With iron he dug through a steep rock and built reservoirs for water.
In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh, and he departed. He raised his hand against Zion and boasted greatly in his arrogance.
Then their hearts and hands were shaken, and they suffered pangs like women giving birth.
They called upon the merciful Lord, spreading their hands toward Him. The Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and redeemed them by Isaiah’s hand.
He struck the Assyrians’ camp, and His angel destroyed them.
For Hezekiah did what was pleasing to the Lord and stood strong in the ways of his father David, which Isaiah the prophet commanded, great and faithful in his vision.
In his days the sun went backward, and He added life to the king.
With a great spirit he saw the last things and comforted those mourning in Zion.
He showed what would happen to the end of the age, and hidden things before they came to pass.
The remembrance of Josiah is like a blend of incense prepared by a perfumer’s skill. In every mouth it will be sweet as honey, and like music at a wine banquet.
He was rightly directed in bringing the people back, and he removed the abominations of lawlessness.
He directed his heart toward the Lord; in days of lawless people he strengthened godliness.
Except for David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, they all committed offenses. For they abandoned the law of the Most High; the kings of Judah came to an end.
For they gave their horn to others and their glory to a foreign nation.
They burned the chosen city of the sanctuary and made its streets desolate,
by Jeremiah’s hand. For they mistreated him, though he was sanctified in the womb as a prophet to uproot, afflict, and destroy, and likewise to build and plant.
Ezekiel saw a vision of glory, which He showed him upon a chariot of cherubim.
For He remembered the enemies in a rainstorm, and remembered to do good to those who make their ways straight.
May the bones of the twelve prophets flourish again from their place! For they comforted Jacob and redeemed them with the faithfulness of hope.
How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He too was like a seal upon the right hand.
So was Joshua son of Jozadak. In their days they built a house and raised up a holy sanctuary for the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.
Great also is the remembrance of Nehemiah, who raised our fallen walls, set up gates and bars, and rebuilt our home sites.
No one was created on earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth.
Nor was a man born like Joseph, a leader of his brothers, a support for the people; and his bones were cared for.
Shem and Seth were glorified among people, and Adam above every living creature in creation.
Simon son of Onias, the high priest, repaired the house in his lifetime and strengthened the sanctuary in his days.
By him the height of the double wall was founded, a high retaining wall around the sacred precinct.
In his days a water reservoir was hewn out, a cistern whose circumference was like a sea.
He cared for his people against a fall and strengthened the city against a siege.
How glorious he was with the people surrounding him, when he came out from the house of the veil!
He was like the morning star among clouds, like the full moon in its days,
like the sun shining upon the sanctuary of the Most High, and like the rainbow gleaming in clouds of glory,
like a rose blossom in the days of new growth, like lilies beside an outflow of water, like a shoot of Lebanon in summer days,
like fire and frankincense upon a firepan, like a vessel of beaten gold adorned with every costly stone,
like an olive tree flourishing with fruit, and like a cypress rising into the clouds.
When he took up the robe of glory and clothed himself with the fullness of splendor, as he ascended the holy altar he glorified the sanctuary’s enclosure.

When he received portions from the priests’ hands, standing himself beside the altar hearth, a crown of brothers surrounded him, like a growth of cedars in Lebanon; they encircled him like palm trunks,
all the sons of Aaron in their glory, with the Lord’s offering in their hands before the whole assembly of Israel.
As he completed his ministry at the altars, adorning the offering of the Most High Almighty,
he stretched his hand over the libation vessel and poured a drink offering from the blood of the grape. He poured it at the altar’s foundations, a pleasing fragrance to the Most High, King of all.
Then the sons of Aaron cried out and sounded their hammered trumpets. They made a great sound heard as a remembrance before the Most High.
Then all the people together hurried and fell facedown upon the earth to worship their Lord, the Almighty God Most High.
The psalm singers praised with their voices; amid a very great sound the melody grew sweet.
The people entreated the Lord Most High in prayer before the Merciful One, until the Lord’s ceremony was completed and they finished His service.
Then he came down and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, to give the Lord’s blessing from his lips and to glory in His name.
They bowed down a second time to receive the blessing from the Most High.
And now bless the God of all, who does great things everywhere, who exalts our days from the womb and deals with us according to His mercy.
May He give us gladness of heart, and may there be peace in Israel in our days, throughout the days of eternity.
May He entrust His mercy to us, and in our days may He redeem us.
My soul is disgusted with two nations, and the third is no nation:
those who sit on Mount Samaria, the Philistines, and the foolish people who dwell in Shechem.
Jesus son of Sirach Eleazar, the Jerusalemite, inscribed instruction in understanding and knowledge in this book; he poured wisdom like rain from his heart.
Blessed is the one who will occupy himself with these things; by setting them upon his heart he will become wise.
For if he does them, he will be strong for everything, because the Lord’s light is his path.
I will give thanks to Thee, Lord and King, and praise Thee, God my Savior. I give thanks to Thy name,

because Thou didst become my shelter and helper. Thou didst redeem my body from destruction and from the snare of a slanderous tongue, from lips that work falsehood. Before those standing around, Thou didst become my helper and redeem me,
according to the abundance of Thy mercy and Thy name, from gnashing teeth when I was ready to be devoured, from the hand of those seeking my life, from the many afflictions I had,
from the choking of a fire all around, and from the midst of a fire that I did not kindle,
from the depth of Hades’ belly, from an unclean tongue and a false word—
slander to a king from an unjust tongue. My soul drew near to death, and my life was close to Hades below.
They surrounded me on every side, and there was no helper. I looked for support from people, but there was none.
I remembered Thy mercy, Lord, and Thy work from of old: Thou rescuest those who wait for Thee and savest them from the hand of enemies.
I lifted my supplication from the earth and pleaded for deliverance from death.

I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, not to abandon me in days of affliction, in a time of arrogance when there was no help. I will praise Thy name continually and sing hymns with thanksgiving.
My petition was heard, for Thou didst save me from destruction and rescue me from an evil time.
Therefore I will give thanks to Thee and praise Thee and bless the Lord’s name.
While I was still young, before I wandered, I openly sought wisdom in my prayer.
Before the sanctuary I asked for her, and until the end I will seek her out.
From her blossom, as from a ripening grape, my heart rejoiced in her. My foot stepped in uprightness; from my youth I traced her path.
I inclined my ear a little and received, and found much instruction for myself.
I made progress in her; I will give glory to the One who gives me wisdom.
For I resolved to practice her and was zealous for the good, and I will never be put to shame.
My soul has struggled for her, and I was exact in practicing the law. I spread my hands toward the height and mourned my soul’s unwitting faults.
I directed my soul toward her and found her in purity. From the beginning I gained a heart together with her; therefore I will never be abandoned.
My inward parts were stirred to seek her out; therefore I acquired a good possession.
The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward, and with it I will praise Him.
Draw near to me, you who are uninstructed, and lodge in a house of instruction.
Why do you say you are lacking in these things, while your souls thirst exceedingly?
I opened my mouth and said, “Acquire for yourselves without silver.
“Put your neck beneath the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction. She is near at hand to be found.
“See with your own eyes that I labored a little and found much rest for myself.
“Take part in instruction at the cost of much silver, and acquire much gold through her.
“May your soul rejoice in His mercy, and may you not be ashamed in His praise.
“Do your work before the appointed time, and He will give you your reward in His time.”
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: Take unto yourself Joshua son of Nun, a man who has spirit within him, and you shall lay your hands upon him,
and shall set him before Eleazar the priest, and shall instruct him before all the congregation, and shall give instructions concerning him before them,
and shall put of your glory upon him, that the sons of Israel may obey him.

And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and they shall ask him for the judgment of the manifestations before the Lord. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in: he, the sons of Israel together, and the whole congregation.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
And he laid his hands on him and presented him, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
After the death of Moses, the Lord spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ attendant, saying:
“Moses My servant has died. Now therefore arise and cross the Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving them.
Every place where you tread with the sole of your feet I will give you, as I have spoken to Moses.
The wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river, the River Euphrates, and as far as the furthest sea toward the setting sun shall be your borders.
No man shall withstand you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not forsake you or disregard you.
Be strong and courageous, for you shall apportion to this people the land which I swore to your fathers to give them.

Be strong and courageous, then, to keep and do what Moses My servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from these commands to the right or to the left, so that you may have understanding in all that you do.

This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand how to do all that is written. Then you shall prosper and make your ways prosper, and then you shall understand.
Behold, I have commanded you: be strong and courageous. Do not be fainthearted or afraid, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua took all the land, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua gave these as an inheritance to Israel, in a division according to their tribes. And the land ceased being at war.
And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, among those who had explored the land, tore their garments.
And they said to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel: The land we inspected is exceedingly, exceedingly good.
If the Lord chooses us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not become deserters from the Lord. Do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. Their season has passed away from them, but the Lord is among us. Do not fear them.
And the whole congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the Lord’s glory appeared in a cloud over the Tent of Testimony among all the sons of Israel.
But My servant Caleb, because a different spirit was in him and he followed Me, I will bring into the land he entered, and his seed shall inherit it.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And I will bring into the land the children whom you said would become plunder, and they shall inherit the land from which you turned away.
And your bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
But your sons shall live as herders in the wilderness for forty years and bear your whoredom, until your bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
According to the number of days you searched out the land—forty days, a day for a year—you shall bear your sins for forty years, and you shall know the fury of My anger.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I will certainly do this to this evil congregation that has banded together against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
And this was the registration by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who registered the sons of Israel in Araboth of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And among these there was no man from those registered by Moses and Aaron, when they registered the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the Lord had said of them: They shall certainly die in the wilderness. Not one of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The sons of Judah drew near to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know the word that the Lord spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea.
For I was forty years old when Moses the servant of God sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I answered him with a report according to his mind.
But my brothers who went up with me turned away the heart of the people; yet I gave myself to follow the Lord my God.
Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘The land on which you have trodden shall be a lot for you and your children for ever, for you gave yourself to follow the Lord our God.’

Now the Lord has sustained me, as He said. This is the forty-fifth year since the Lord spoke this word to Moses and Israel journeyed in the wilderness. And now, look: today I am eighty-five years old.
I am still strong today, as when Moses sent me; I am just as strong now to go out and come in for war.

Now I ask you for this mountain, as the Lord said on that day, for you heard this word on that day. The Anakim are now there, and great, fortified cities. If the Lord is with me, I shall destroy them, as the Lord said to me.”
Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh son of Kenaz as a lot.
Therefore Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as a lot to this day, because he followed the command of the Lord, the God of Israel.
The former name of Hebron was the city of Arbok; it was the mother-city of the Anakim. And the land grew quiet from war.
To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the sons of Judah by God’s command, and Joshua gave him the city of Arbok, the mother-city of Anak—that is Hebron.
Caleb son of Jephunneh destroyed from there the three sons of Anak: Sousi, Talmai, and Achima.
Caleb went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir; Debir’s former name was City of Letters.
Caleb said, “Whoever takes and cuts down the City of Letters and gains mastery over it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as a wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it, and he gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
When she entered, she consulted with him, saying, “I will ask my father for a field.” She cried out from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What is it?”
And she said to him, “Give me a blessing; for you have given me to the land of Negeb. Give me Golathmaim.” And Caleb gave her Upper Golathmaim and Lower Golathmaim.
The Lord raised up judges for them and saved them from the hand of their plunderers.

Yet they did not listen even to their judges, for they prostituted themselves after other gods, bowed down to them, and provoked the Lord. They quickly turned aside from the way their fathers had walked in obeying the Lord’s commandments. They did not do as their fathers had done.

Whenever the Lord raised up judges for them, the Lord was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge. For the Lord was moved by their groaning before those who besieged and harmed them.

When the judge died, they turned back and again acted more corruptly than their fathers, following other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They did not cast away their practices or depart from their hard way.
And what more shall I say? For time will fail me as I recount Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets,
who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
extinguished the power of fire, escaped the edges of the sword, were strengthened from weakness, became mighty in battle, and turned back the armies of foreigners.
You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will spring up like vegetation. The Lord’s hand will be known to those who revere Him, and He will threaten the disobedient.
The memory of righteous people is with praises, but the name of the impious is extinguished.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or lose heart. Take all the men of war with you, arise, and go up to Ai. Behold, I have delivered the king of Ai and his land into your hands.
Do to Ai as you did to Jericho and its king, and take the livestock as spoil for yourself. Set an ambush behind the city.”
Joshua and all the fighting people arose to go up to Ai. Joshua selected thirty thousand mighty men and sent them away by night.
He commanded them, “Lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go far from the city, and all of you be ready.
I and everyone with me will approach the city. When Ai’s inhabitants come out to meet us as before, we shall flee before them.
When they come out after us, we shall draw them away from the city. They will say, ‘These men are fleeing before us as before.’
Then rise from the ambush and go into the city.
Do according to this word. Behold, I have commanded you.”
Joshua sent them away, and they went to the ambush and took their position between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai.
Joshua rose early in the morning and inspected the people. He and the elders went up before the people toward Ai.
All the fighting people with him went up and came opposite the city from the east,
while the ambush lay west of the city.
When the king of Ai saw, he hurried straight out to meet them in battle, he and all the people with him. He did not know there was an ambush behind the city.
Joshua saw and withdrew, and Israel withdrew before them.
They pursued the sons of Israel and moved away from the city.
No one remained in Ai who did not pursue Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Stretch out your hand with the javelin you hold toward the city, for I have delivered it into your hands. The ambush shall rise quickly from its place.” Joshua stretched out his hand, with the javelin, toward the city,
and the ambush rose quickly from its place. They came out when he stretched out his hand, went to the city, captured it, and hurried to burn it with fire.
Ai’s inhabitants looked behind them and saw smoke rising from the city toward heaven. They no longer had anywhere to flee, this way or that.
Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that its smoke rose toward heaven. They turned and struck Ai’s men.
The others came out of the city to meet them, and they were caught between the forces, some on this side and some on that. They struck them until no survivor or fugitive remained.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When the sons of Israel finished killing all Ai’s people in the plains and on the mountain, on the descent where they pursued them from it to the end, Joshua returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
Those who fell that day, men and women, were twelve thousand, all Ai’s inhabitants,
except the livestock and the spoil in the city, all of which the sons of Israel took as plunder according to the Lord’s command, as the Lord had directed Joshua.
Joshua burned the city with fire and made it an uninhabited mound for ever, as it remains to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a forked tree, and he remained on the tree until evening. At sunset Joshua gave the command, and they took his body down from the tree. They threw him into the pit and set a heap of stones over him, which remains to this day.

Adoni-bezek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Ai and destroyed it. As they had done to Jericho and its king, so they had done to Ai and its king. He also heard that Gibeon’s inhabitants had gone over to Joshua and Israel.
They were greatly afraid of them, for he knew that Gibeon was a great city, like one of the chief cities, and all its men were strong.
Adoni-bezek king of Jerusalem sent to Ailam king of Hebron, Pheidon king of Jarmuth, Jephtha king of Lachish, and Debir king of Adullam, saying:
“Come up to me and help me. Let us wage war on Gibeon, for they have gone over to Joshua and the sons of Israel.”
The five kings of the Jebusites—of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Adullam—went up with all their people. They surrounded Gibeon and besieged it.

The inhabitants of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp of Israel in Gilgal, saying, “Do not withdraw your hands from your servants. Come up to us quickly, and save us and help us; for all the kings of the Amorites dwelling in the hill country are gathered against us.”
Joshua went up from Gilgal with all the fighting people, every mighty man of strength.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. None of them shall remain before you.”
Joshua arrived against them suddenly, having travelled from Gilgal the whole night.

The Lord threw them into confusion before the sons of Israel, and the Lord crushed them with a great defeat at Gibeon. They pursued them along the ascent of Horonin and cut them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before the sons of Israel down the descent of Horonin, the Lord hurled hailstones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah. More died from the hailstones than the sons of Israel killed with the sword in battle.

Then Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day God handed the Amorites over to Israel, when He crushed them at Gibeon and they were crushed before the sons of Israel. Joshua said, “Let the sun stand over Gibeon, and the moon over the ravine of Aijalon.”
The sun stood, and the moon remained still, until God repelled their enemies. The sun stood in the middle of heaven and did not advance toward sunset for a full day.
There was no such day before or afterward, when God listened to a human being, for the Lord fought alongside Israel.
These five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was informed, “The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua said, “Roll stones against the mouth of the cave and station men over them to keep watch.
Do not stop pursuing your enemies. Overtake their rear guard, and do not let them enter their cities; for the Lord our God has delivered them into our hands.”
When Joshua and every son of Israel had finished cutting them down in a very great slaughter to the end, those who escaped reached the fortified cities.
Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and none of his words fell to the ground.
All Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was faithful as a prophet to the Lord.

The Lord continued to make Himself known at Shiloh, for the Lord revealed Himself to Samuel. Samuel was recognized as a prophet of the Lord for all Israel, from the ends of the land to the ends. Eli was very old, and his sons continued on their way, and their way was evil before the Lord.

Samuel said to all Israel’s house, “If you are returning to the Lord with all your heart, remove the foreign gods and the groves from among you. Prepare your hearts toward the Lord and serve Him alone, and He will rescue you from the foreigners’ hand.”
The sons of Israel removed the Baalim and the groves of Astaroth and served the Lord alone.
Samuel said, “Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
They gathered at Mizpah, drew water, and poured it onto the ground before the Lord. They fasted that day and said, “We have sinned before the Lord.” Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.
The foreigners heard that all the sons of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, and the foreigners’ satraps went up against Israel. When the sons of Israel heard, they were afraid of the foreigners.
The sons of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not be silent on our behalf: keep crying to the Lord your God, and He will save us from the foreigners’ hand.”
Samuel took one nursing lamb and, with all the people, offered it as a whole burnt offering to the Lord. Samuel cried to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.

While Samuel was offering the whole burnt offering, the foreigners drew near for battle against Israel. The Lord thundered with a great voice against the foreigners that day. They were thrown into confusion and fell before Israel.
Israel’s men went out from Mizpah, pursued the foreigners, and struck them as far as below Beth-chor.
Samuel took one stone and set it between Mizpah and the old city. He named it Ebenezer, Stone of the Helper, and said, “Thus far the Lord has helped us.”
The Lord humbled the foreigners, and they did not enter Israel’s territory again. The Lord’s hand was against the foreigners throughout Samuel’s days.

The cities that the foreigners had taken from the sons of Israel were restored; they returned them to Israel, from Ashkelon to Azob. They recovered Israel’s territory from the foreigners’ hand. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
Samuel judged Israel throughout his life.
Year after year he traveled a circuit through Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, judging Israel in all these consecrated places.
He would return to Armathaim, for his house was there. There he judged Israel, and there he built an altar to the Lord.

Samuel took the flask of oil, poured it on his head, kissed him, and said to him, “Has not the Lord anointed you as ruler over His people, over Israel? You will rule among the Lord’s people and save them from their enemies’ hand all around. This will be the sign to you that the Lord has anointed you as ruler over His inheritance:

The Lord said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn over Saul, when I have treated him as nothing so that he should not reign over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and come. I will send you to Jesse, to Bethlehem, for I have seen one among his sons to reign for Me.”
Samuel said, “How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me.” The Lord said, “Take a heifer in your hand and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.’
Invite Jesse to the sacrifice. I will make known to you what you must do, and you shall anoint the one I name to you.”
Samuel did everything the Lord had spoken to him and came to Bethlehem. The city’s elders were terrified at meeting him and said, “Do you enter in peace, seer?”
He said, “In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Consecrate yourselves and rejoice with me today.” He consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
When they came in, he saw Eliab and said, “Surely His anointed is before the Lord.”

The Lord said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or the bearing of his height, for I have treated him as nothing. God does not see as a human looks: a human looks at the face, but God looks at the heart.”
Jesse called Aminadab, and he passed before Samuel. He said, “The Lord has not chosen this one either.”
Jesse made Shammah pass by. He said, “The Lord has not chosen this one either.”
Jesse made his seven sons pass before Samuel. Samuel said, “The Lord has not chosen among these.”

Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the boys?” He said, “There is still the youngest; he is tending the flock.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and fetch him, for we will certainly not recline until he comes.”
He sent and brought him. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look upon before the Lord. The Lord said to Samuel, “Rise and anoint David, for this one is good.”
Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers. The Lord’s Spirit leaped upon David from that day onward. Samuel rose and went to Armathaim.
Samuel said to every man of Israel, “Behold, I have listened to your voice in everything you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
Now the king walks before you. I have grown old and will sit down, and my sons are here among you. I have walked before you from my youth to this day.

Here I am. Answer against me before the Lord and before His anointed: Whose calf have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Which of you have I tyrannized? Whom have I squeezed? From whose hand have I taken an appeasing payment and a sandal? Answer against me, and I will repay you.”
They said to Samuel, “You have not wronged us or tyrannized us or crushed us, and you have taken nothing from anyone’s hand.”
Samuel said to the people, “The Lord is witness among you, and His anointed is witness today, on this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.” They said, “Witness.”
The woman said, “Whom shall I bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”
The woman saw Samuel and cried out with a loud voice. The woman said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
The king said to her, “Do not fear. Tell me whom you have seen.” She said to him, “I have seen gods coming up from the earth.”

He said to her, “What did you perceive?” She said to him, “A man standing upright is coming up from the earth, wrapped in a double cloak.” Saul knew that this was Samuel, and he bent with his face to the ground and bowed to him.

Samuel said, “Why have you troubled me, that I should come up?” Saul said, “I am greatly afflicted. The foreigners are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and no longer listens to me, either through the prophets or by dreams. Now I have called you to make known to me what I should do.”
Samuel said, “Why do you inquire of me, when the Lord has departed from you and has come to be with your neighbour?
The Lord has done to you as He spoke by my hand. The Lord will tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your neighbour David.
Because you did not listen to the Lord’s voice and did not carry out His furious anger against Amalek, the Lord has done this thing to you this day.
The Lord will hand Israel with you into the foreigners’ hands. Tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall. The Lord will give Israel’s camp into the foreigners’ hands.”
And he slept. As dawn came up, Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Arise, and I will send you away.” Saul got up, and he and Samuel went outside.
As they went down toward the side of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the young man to go ahead of us. But you stand here a while and hear God’s word.”

When you leave me today, you will find two men near Rachel’s tombs in Benjamin’s territory, leaping greatly. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you both went to seek have been found. Your father has cast aside the matter of the donkeys and has spent lavishly on your account, saying, “What shall I do for my son?”’
The dancing women came out from all Israel’s cities to meet David, with tambourines, joy, and cymbals.
The women led the song and said, “Saul has struck his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
The saying appeared evil in Saul’s eyes concerning this matter, and he said, “They have given David the tens of thousands, but to me they have given the thousands.”
Saul kept looking askance at David from that day onward.
The foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David. David heard and went down to the stronghold.
The foreigners arrived and gathered in the Valley of the Titans.

David inquired through the Lord, saying, “Shall I go up against the foreigners? Wilt Thou deliver them into my hands?” The Lord said to David, “Go up, for I will certainly deliver the foreigners into your hands.”

David came from the Upper Breaches and struck the foreigners there. David said, “The Lord has broken through my enemies, the foreigners, before me as waters break through.” Therefore that place was named Upper Breaches.
They abandoned their gods there, and David and the men with him took them.
The foreigners came up again and gathered in the Valley of the Titans.
David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, “Do not go up to meet them. Turn away from them, and you will come upon them near the place of weeping.
When you hear the sound of the closing together of the grove of weeping, then go down against them, for then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle with the foreigners.”
David did as the Lord commanded him and struck the foreigners from Gibeon as far as the land of Gezer.
After this, David struck the foreigners and routed them. David took the separated territory from the foreigners’ hand.
When the king was settled in his house and the Lord had given him possession on every side, away from all his surrounding enemies,
the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look now, I dwell in a cedar house, while the ark of God remains inside the tent.”
Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you.”
That night a word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
“Go and say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the Lord: You will not build Me a house for Me to dwell in,
for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt until this day. I have been moving about in a lodging and a tent.
Wherever I passed through among all Israel, did I ever speak to one of Israel’s tribes whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, “Why have you not built Me a cedar house?”
Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people, over Israel,
and I was with you wherever you went and destroyed all your enemies before you, and I made you renowned, according to the name of the great ones on the earth.
I will appoint a place for My people Israel and plant them there. They will dwell on their own and worry no more. No unjust man will again humble them as at the beginning,
from the days when I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will announce to you that you will build Him a house.
When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your own body, and prepare his kingdom.
He will build Me a house for My name, and I will set his throne upright for ever.
I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. If his wrongdoing comes, I will correct him with the rod of men and the afflictions of human beings.
But I will not withdraw My mercy from him as I withdrew it from those whom I removed from before Me.
His house and his kingdom will be made sure for ever before Me, and his throne will be set upright for ever.’”
Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and all this vision.
David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the Lord.” Nathan said to David, “The Lord also has put away your sin; you will certainly not die.
He appointed some Levites to minister before the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to sound out, give thanks, and praise the Lord, Israel’s God:
Asaph the leader, Zacharias second to him, Jiiel, Semiramoth, Jiiel, Mattathias, Eliab, Banaias, Abdedom, and Jiiel, with instruments, harps, and lyres; Asaph sounded the cymbals.
Banaias and Oziel the priests sounded trumpets continually before the ark of God’s covenant.
On that day David first appointed praise of the Lord through Asaph and his brethren:
They left Asaph and his brethren there before the ark of the Lord’s covenant to minister continually before the ark, each day’s duty on its day,
with Abdedom and his brethren, sixty-eight; Abdedom son of Idithon and Ossa were gatekeepers.
They left Sadok the priest and his brother priests before the Lord’s tent at Bama in Gabaon,

to present whole burnt offerings to the Lord continually on the altar of whole burnt offerings, morning and evening, according to everything written in the Lord’s law, all He commanded Israel’s sons through Moses, God’s attendant;
With him were Aiman, Idithon, and the remaining men chosen by name, to praise the Lord, for His mercy endures for ever.
With them were trumpets and cymbals for sounding out, and instruments for God’s songs; Idithon’s sons were at the gate.
All the people went, each to his house, and David returned to bless his household.
and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks unto the Lord, and likewise in the evening;
and over all the whole burnt offerings offered to the Lord on sabbaths, new moons, and feasts, by number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually for the Lord.
David lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
David’s reign over Israel lasted forty years. He reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
Solomon sat on the throne of his father David when he was twelve years old, and his kingdom was firmly prepared.
The foreigners gathered their camps for war and assembled at Soccoth in Judea. They camped between Soccoth and Azekah at Epher-mem.
Saul and Israel’s men gathered and camped in the valley. They drew up for war opposite the foreigners.
The foreigners stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other, with the ravine between them.
A mighty man came out from the foreigners’ battle line, named Goliath, from Gath. His height was four cubits and a span.
A helmet was on his head, and he wore a coat of chain armour. His armour’s weight was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron.
Bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders.
His spear’s shaft was like a weavers’ beam, and its iron head weighed six hundred shekels. The one carrying his weapons walked before him.

He stood and shouted to Israel’s battle line, “Why have you come out to draw up for war opposite us? Am I not a foreigner, and are you not Saul’s Hebrews? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to me.
If he can fight me and strike me down, we will become your slaves. But if I prevail and strike him down, you will become our slaves and serve us.”
The foreigner said, “Behold, I have defied Israel’s battle line today, on this day. Give me a man, and let the two of us fight in single combat.”
Saul and all Israel heard these words of the foreigner and were terrified and exceedingly afraid.
David said to Saul, “Let my lord’s heart not collapse because of him. Your servant will go and fight this foreigner.”
Saul said to David, “You certainly cannot go against the foreigner to fight him. You are a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
David said to Saul, “Your servant tended his father’s flock. Whenever a lion or a bear came and took a sheep from the herd,
I went after it, struck it, and pulled the sheep from its mouth. If it rose against me, I seized its throat, struck it, and killed it.

Your servant struck both bear and lion. The uncircumcised foreigner will be like one of them. Shall I not go and strike him and remove disgrace from Israel today? For who is this uncircumcised man who has defied the battle line of the living God?
The Lord, who rescued me from the lion’s paw and the bear’s paw, will rescue me from this uncircumcised foreigner’s hand.” Saul said to David, “Go, and the Lord will be with you.”
Saul clothed David in a cloak and set a bronze helmet around his head.
He strapped his sword on David over his cloak. David became weary after walking once or twice. David said to Saul, “I certainly cannot walk in these, for I am not practiced.” They took them off him.

He took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in the shepherd’s little vessel he had for collecting. His sling was in his hand, and he approached the foreign man.
Goliath saw David and dishonoured him, for he was a boy, ruddy, with beautiful eyes.
The foreigner said to David, “Am I like a dog, that you come against me with a staff and stones?” David said, “No, you are worse than a dog.” The foreigner cursed David by his gods.
The foreigner said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of heaven and the animals of the land.”
David said to the foreigner, “You come to me with sword, spear, and shield. I come to you in the name of the Lord Sabaoth, God of Israel’s battle line, which you have defied today.

This day the Lord will shut you into my hand. I will kill you and remove your head from you. This day I will give your limbs and the limbs of the foreigners’ camp to the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
All this assembly will know that the Lord does not save by sword and spear. The battle belongs to the Lord, and the Lord will hand you all into our hands.”
The foreigner rose and went to meet David.

David reached his hand into the little vessel, took one stone from it, slung it, and struck the foreigner on his forehead. The stone passed through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell face down to the ground.
David ran and stood over him, took his sword, killed him, and removed his head. When the foreigners saw that their mighty man was dead, they fled.
Israel’s and Judah’s men rose with a shout and pursued them as far as Gath’s entrance and Ashkelon’s gate. Wounded foreigners fell along the road of the gates, as far as Gath and Ekron.
Israel’s men turned back from following the foreigners and trampled their camps.
David took the foreigner’s head and brought it to Jerusalem. He placed his equipment in his tent.

The appointed officers thus provided for King Solomon and all the orders for the king’s table, each in his month; they did not depart from an instruction. They brought barley and straw for the horses and chariots to the place where the king would be, each according to his assignment.
These were Solomon’s requirements for one day: thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of pounded meal,
ten choice calves, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, and choice birds—fattened provisions.
For he was ruler beyond the River, and he had peace on every side around him.
The Lord gave Solomon discernment, very great wisdom, and abundance of heart like the sand beside the sea.
Solomon increased greatly beyond the discernment of all ancient people and beyond all the discerning people of Egypt.
He became wiser than all people; he became wiser than Gaithan the Ezraite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mal.
Solomon spoke three thousand parables, and his songs numbered five thousand.
He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing through the wall. He spoke about livestock, birds, creeping things, and fish.
All the peoples came to hear Solomon’s wisdom, and he received gifts from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
Solomon took Pharaoh’s daughter as his wife and brought her into the City of David until he finished the Lord’s house, his own house, and Jerusalem’s wall.

Then Pharaoh king of Egypt went up, captured Gezer beforehand, and burned it and the Canaanite who lived in Mergab. Pharaoh gave them as parting gifts to his daughter, Solomon’s wife; and Solomon built Gezer.
Hiram king of Tyre sent his attendants to anoint Solomon in place of David his father, for Hiram had always loved David.
Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,
“You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the Lord put them beneath the footsteps of his feet.
But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side; there is no plotter and no evil encounter.

Behold, I intend to build a house for the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord God told my father David: ‘Your son, whom I shall place on your throne in your place, shall build the house for My name.’

Now command that they cut timber from Lebanon for me. Behold, my servants are with your servants, and I will pay you the wages of your service according to whatever you say; for you know that no one among us knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”
When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be God this day, who has given David a discerning son over this great people!”
He sent to Solomon, saying, “I have heard about everything you did send to me. I will fulfill all your wishes: cedar and pine timber.

My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea. I will make them into rafts as far as the place you send me word about, and shake them apart there; you shall take them away. You shall fulfill my wish by providing loaves for my household.”
Hiram supplied Solomon with cedars and all that he desired.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat and machir for his household, and twenty thousand beth of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram each year.
The Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a covenant between themselves.
The king raised a levy from all Israel; the levy was thirty thousand men.
He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in shifts: one month they were in Lebanon and two months at their home. Adoniram was over the levy.
Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
besides the chiefs appointed over Solomon’s works, three thousand six hundred overseers who performed the works.
They prepared the stones and timber for three years.
And from the sacrifice of deliverance they shall bring an offering unto the Lord: the fat which covers the belly, and all the fat upon the belly,
and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer them up upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offerings, upon the wood upon the fire upon the altar: an offering, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
David said to Solomon, “Child, it came upon my soul to build a house for the name of the Lord God.

But the Lord’s word came upon me, saying, ‘You have poured out much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for My name, because you have poured out much blood upon the earth before Me.

Behold, a son is born unto you; he shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all the enemies round about him, for Solomon is his name; and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.
He will build a house for My name. He will be a son to Me, and I will be a Father to him. I will set upright the throne of his kingdom in Israel for ever.’
King David blessed the Lord before the assembly, saying, “Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting to everlasting.
Thine, O Lord, are greatness, power, glory, victory, and strength; for Thou rulest all things in heaven and upon earth. Before Thee every king and nation is shaken.
From Thee come wealth and glory. Thou governest all, O Lord, Ruler of every rule. In Thy hand are strength and dominion; and it is in Thy hand, O Almighty, to make all things great and strong.
Now, O Lord, we give thanks unto Thee, and praise the name of Thy glory.
The Lord appeared to Solomon in sleep at night. The Lord said to Solomon, “Ask a request for yourself.”

Solomon said, “Thou showedst great mercy to Thy servant David my father, as he walked before Thee in truth, righteousness, and uprightness of heart with Thee. Thou keptest this great mercy for him, placing his son on his throne, as it is this day.
Now, Lord my God, Thou hast placed Thy servant in place of my father David. I am a little child and do not know my going out or my coming in.
Thy servant is among Thy people whom Thou didst choose, a numerous people who cannot be numbered.
Give Thy servant a heart to hear and to judge Thy people in righteousness, discerning between good and evil; for who can judge this weighty people of Thine?”
It pleased the Lord that Solomon had asked this.
The Lord said to him, “Because you have asked this of Me and have not asked for many days for yourself, or wealth, or the lives of your enemies, but have asked for understanding to hear judgment,
behold, I have done according to your word. Behold, I have given you a discerning and wise heart, so that no one like you has been before you, and no one like you shall arise after you.
I have also given you what you did not ask: both wealth and glory, so that no man like you has been among the kings.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask what I should give you.”
Solomon said to God, “Thou didst show great mercy to David my father, and Thou didst make me king in his place.
Now, Lord God, let Thy name be confirmed upon David my father, for Thou hast made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Now give me wisdom and understanding, and I shall go out before this people and come in; for who can judge this great people of Thine?”

God said to Solomon, “Because this came into your heart, and you did not ask for wealth of possessions, glory, or the life of opponents, and did not ask for many days, but did ask for wisdom and understanding to judge My people over whom I made you king,
I give you wisdom and understanding. I will also give you wealth, possessions, and glory, so that none like you has existed among the kings before you, nor will it be so after you.”
For the end. Of the Lord’s servant David, who spoke the words of this song to the Lord on the day the Lord rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
And he said: I will love Thee, Lord, my strength.
The Lord is my firm foundation, my refuge, and my rescuer; my God is my helper, and I will hope in Him; my protector, the horn of my salvation, my supporter.
Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.
The queen of Sheba heard Solomon’s name and the Lord’s name, and came to test him with riddles.
She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came in to Solomon and spoke to him about everything in her heart.
Solomon explained all her matters to her. No matter was overlooked by the king that he did not explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon’s discernment and the house he had built,
Solomon’s food, the seating of his attendants, the station of his ministers, his clothing, his wine-pourers, and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the Lord’s house, she was beside herself.
She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my land about your word and your discernment is true.
I did not believe those speaking to me until I arrived and my eyes saw. Behold, it is not half as they reported to me! You have added good things beyond them, beyond every report I heard in my land.
Blessed are your women! Blessed are these attendants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your discernment!

Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you, setting you on Israel’s throne! Because the Lord loves Israel, to establish them for ever, He made you king over them to carry out judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.”
The weight of gold coming to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
besides the tribute of the subject peoples, the merchants, all the kings of the region beyond, and the satraps of the land.
Solomon made three hundred spears of hammered gold; three hundred gold pieces went onto each spear.
He also made three hundred shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold were in each shield. He placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with tested gold.
The throne had six steps, foreparts of calves behind it, and arms on each side of the seat, with two lions standing beside the arms.
Twelve lions stood on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.

All Solomon’s drinking vessels were gold, and the basins were gold. All the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were encased in gold. None were silver, because silver was not valued in Solomon’s days.
For the king had a Tarshish ship at sea with Hiram’s ships. Once every three years a ship came to the king from Tarshish with gold, silver, and engraved and hewn stones.

This was the undertaking for the spoil which King Solomon brought up: to build the Lord’s house, the king’s house, Jerusalem’s wall, and the citadel, to enclose the enclosure of the City of David; also Assour, Magdan, Gezer, Upper Beth-horon, Iethermath, all the chariot cities, all the horsemen’s cities, and Solomon’s undertaking which he undertook to build in Jerusalem and throughout the land, so that there might not rule over him

any of the people remaining from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites, who were not of the sons of Israel—their children remaining after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had been unable to destroy. Solomon subjected them to tribute, as it remains to this day.
But Solomon put none of the sons of Israel into labor, because they were his warriors and attendants, his chariot commanders and his horsemen.
Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in wealth and discernment.
All the kings of the earth sought Solomon’s presence to hear the discernment the Lord had put in his heart.
Each brought his gifts: gold vessels, clothing, stacte, spices, horses, and mules, year after year.
Solomon had four thousand mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. He placed the mares in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the foreigners and to Egypt’s borders.
The king made gold and silver in Jerusalem as common as stones, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamores in the plain.

The queen of Saba heard Solomon’s name and came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with riddles, with a very great force and camels carrying spices, plentiful gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke to him about everything in her soul.
Solomon explained all her questions to her. No matter escaped Solomon that he did not explain to her.
When the queen of Saba saw Solomon’s wisdom and the house he had built,

the food of the tables, the seating of his servants, the station of his ministers and their clothing, his wine-pourers and their attire, and the whole burnt offerings he offered in the Lord’s house, she was beside herself.
She said to the king, “The report I heard in my land about your words and wisdom was true.
I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes saw. Behold, not half the abundance of your wisdom was reported to me! You surpass the report I heard.
Happy are the men, happy are these servants of yours who stand by you continually and hear your wisdom!
All King Solomon’s vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were covered with gold. Silver was considered of no account in Solomon’s days.
For a ship belonging to the king traveled to Tharsis with Chiram’s servants. Once every three years ships came from Tharsis to the king, laden with gold, silver, elephant tusks, and apes.
Solomon became greater than all the kings in both wealth and wisdom.
All earth’s kings sought Solomon’s presence to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
Each brought his gifts: silver vessels, gold vessels, clothing, stacte, aromatic spices, horses, and mules, year after year.
Solomon had four thousand mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. He stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
He was leader over all the kings from the River to the foreigners’ land and to Egypt’s border.
The king made gold and silver in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars as plentiful as sycamores in the plain.

King Solomon was a lover of women. He had seven hundred princesses and three hundred concubines. He took foreign wives, as well as Pharaoh’s daughter: Moabite, Ammonite, Syrian, Edomite, Hittite, and Amorite women,

from the nations about which the Lord had forbidden the sons of Israel, “You shall not go in among them, and they shall not come in among you, lest they turn your hearts after their idols.” Solomon clung to these in love.
When Solomon was old, his heart was not whole with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father; the foreign wives turned his heart after their gods.

[5] Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, Moab’s idol, and for their king, the idol of the sons of Ammon, [6] and for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians. [7] He did the same for all his foreign wives; they burned incense and offered sacrifices to their idols. [8] Solomon did evil before the Lord; he did not walk after the Lord as David his father did.
The Lord became angry with Solomon because he had turned his heart away from the Lord, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had commanded him about this matter, absolutely not to follow other gods, and to take care to do what the Lord God had commanded him.

The Lord said to Solomon, “Because these things have been your conduct, and you have not kept My commandments and My ordinances which I commanded you, I will surely tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your servant.
Yet I will not do these things in your days, because of David your father. I will take it from your son’s hand.
But I will certainly not take the whole kingdom. I will give your son one scepter, because of David My servant and because of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen.”
The king instructed the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was still alive, saying, “How do you advise me, so that I may answer this people?”
They said to him, “If this day you become this people’s servant, serve them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants always.”
He abandoned the elders’ counsel which they had given him and consulted the young men who had been brought up with him and stood before him.
He said to them, “What do you advise, and what shall I answer this people who said to me, ‘Lighten the collar your father placed on us’?”

The young men who had been brought up with him and stood before him said, “Thus speak to this people who told you, ‘Your father made our collar heavy; now lighten it for us.’ Thus speak to them: ‘My little part is thicker than my father’s loins.
Now my father burdened you with a heavy collar, but I will add to your collar. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
All Israel came to King Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them, “Return to me on the third day.”
The king answered the people harshly, and Rehoboam abandoned the elders’ counsel which they had given him.

He spoke to them according to the young men’s counsel: “My father made your collar heavy, but I will add to your collar. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”
The king did not listen to the people, for the turn of events came from the Lord, to establish His word which He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.
