All Israel saw that the king had not listened to them. The people answered the king, “What share have we in David? We have no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Run away to your tents, Israel! Now shepherd your own house, David!” Israel went to their tents.
The king sent Adoniram, who supervised the tribute. All Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. King Rehoboam managed to go up and flee to Jerusalem.
Israel rejected David’s house, as it remains to this day.

When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned from Egypt, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over Israel. None followed David’s house except Judah’s scepter and Benjamin alone.
Jeroboam said in his heart, “Behold, now the kingdom will return to David’s house.
If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the Lord’s house in Jerusalem, the people’s heart will return to the Lord and their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me.”
The king took counsel, went, and made two golden heifers. He said to the people, “Let your going up to Jerusalem be enough. Behold, your gods, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt!”
He placed one in Bethel and put the other in Dan.
This matter became a sin. The people went before the one as far as Dan.
He made houses on high places and appointed some of the people as priests who were not from the sons of Levi.

Jeroboam held a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast in the land of Judah, and went up onto the altar he had made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers he had made. He stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places he had made.

He went up onto the altar he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, at the feast he had fashioned from his heart. He held a feast for the sons of Israel and went up onto the altar to offer sacrifice.
King Rehoboam gathered the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive: “How do you advise answering this people?”
They told him, “If today you are good to this people, show favor, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants all the days.”
He abandoned the elders’ counsel that they had given him and consulted the young men brought up with him who stood before him.
He said to them, “What do you advise, that I may answer this people who said to me, ‘Relax the yoke your father placed upon us’?”

The young men brought up with him told him, “Speak this way to the people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy; you release us from it.’ Say this: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.
My father disciplined you with a heavy yoke; I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said, “Return to me on the third day.”
The king answered harshly. King Rehoboam abandoned the elders’ counsel,
and spoke to them according to the younger men’s counsel: “My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with scorpions.”
The king did not listen to the people, for there was a reversal from God, saying, “The Lord established His word that He spoke through Achia the Selonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nabat

and all Israel,” because the king did not listen to them. The people answered the king: “What share have we in David, and what inheritance in Jesse’s son? To your dwellings, Israel! Now see to your house, David!” All Israel went to their dwellings.

“Did not Salomon king of Israel sin in this way? Among many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women turned even him aside.
“Are we not to hear of you doing all this evil, breaking faith with our God by establishing households with foreign wives?”
This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,
and all the Israelites who clothed themselves in words that were not so against the Lord their God, built themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.
They set up pillars and groves for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
They burned incense there at all the high places like the nations whom the Lord deported before them. They made associates and engraved, to provoke the Lord.
They served the idols, concerning which the Lord had said to them, ‘You shall not do this thing to the Lord.’

The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all His prophets, every seer: ‘Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My ordinances, and all the law I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them through My servants the prophets.’
But they did not listen. They hardened their back more than the back of their fathers.

They did not keep His testimonies by which He warned them. They followed vain things and became vain, and followed the nations around them, concerning whom He had commanded them not to do such things.
They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God. They made a casting for themselves, two heifers, made groves, bowed down to all heaven’s host, and served Baal.
They led their sons and daughters through fire, practiced divinations, read omens, and were sold to do evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.
The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence. None remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God; they walked in the ordinances Israel had made.
They rejected the Lord throughout all Israel’s seed; He shook them and gave them into the hands of those plundering them, until He cast them from His presence.
For Israel was apart from David’s house, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam thrust Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to commit a great sin.
The Israelites walked in every sin Jeroboam committed; they did not turn away from it,
until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, as the Lord had spoken through all His servants the prophets. Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians, to this day.
The Lord swore truth to David, and He will certainly not annul it: “From the fruit of your belly I will set one on your throne.
If your sons keep My covenant and these testimonies of Mine that I will teach them, their sons too will sit for ever on your throne.”
For the Lord chose Zion; He selected her as His dwelling:
“This is My rest for age upon age; here I will dwell, for I selected her.
I will surely bless her game; I will satisfy her poor with loaves.
I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her holy ones will surely exult.
There I will make a horn spring up for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed.
I will clothe his enemies with shame, but upon him My holy sign will blossom.”
For ever I will keep My mercy for him, and My covenant is faithful to him.
I will establish his seed for an age of an age and his throne like the days of heaven.
If his sons abandon My law and do not walk in My judgments,
if they profane My ordinances and do not keep My commandments,
I will visit their lawless acts with a rod and their sins with scourges;
but I shall certainly not scatter My mercy away from him, nor act unjustly in My truth,
nor shall I profane My covenant, and what goes out through My lips I shall certainly not set aside.
Once I swore by My holiness: I will not lie to David.
His seed will remain for ever, and his throne will be like the sun before Me,
and like the moon, established for ever; and the witness in heaven is faithful.” Diapsalma.

Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except through the utterance of my word.”
The Lord’s word came to Elijah:
“Go from here eastward and hide yourself at the Chorrath wadi, which faces the Jordan.
You will drink water from the wadi, and I will command the ravens to sustain you there.”
Elijah acted according to the Lord’s word and stayed at the Chorrath wadi facing the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the wadi.
After some days the wadi dried up, because there had been no rain on the land.
After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill. His illness was very severe, until no breath remained in him.
She said to Elijah, “What have I to do with you, man of God? You have come to me to bring my wrongdoings to remembrance and to put my son to death!”
Elijah said to the woman, “Give me your son.” He took him from her bosom, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
Elijah cried out and said, “Alas, Lord, Witness of the widow with whom I am staying—Thou hast brought harm by putting her son to death!”
He breathed into the child three times, called upon the Lord, and said, “Lord my God, I pray Thee, let this child’s soul return into him!”
It happened so, and the child cried out.
He brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, “Behold, your son lives!”
The woman said to Elijah, “Behold, I know that you are a man of God, and the Lord’s word in your mouth is true.”
After many days, the Lord’s word came to Elijah in the third year, saying, “Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain on the face of the land.”
Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria.

Elijah cried out to heaven and said, “Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, hear me, Lord! Hear me this day with fire, and let all this people know that Thou art the Lord, the God of Israel, and I am Thy servant, and that I have done these works because of Thee.
Hear me, Lord! Hear me with fire, and let this people know that Thou art the Lord God, and that Thou hast turned this people’s heart backward.”
Fire from the Lord fell from heaven and consumed the burnt offering, the split wood, and the water in the trench; the fire licked up the stones and the dust.
All the people fell on their faces and said, “Truly the Lord is God! He is God!”
He rose, ate, and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Mount Horeb.
He entered the cave there and lodged there. Behold, the Lord’s word came to him, and He said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

Elijah said, “I have been most zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the children of Israel have abandoned Thee. They have demolished Thine altars and killed Thy prophets with the sword. I remain utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.”

He said, “You shall go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain. Behold, the Lord will pass by.” A great, strong wind was breaking mountains apart and crushing rocks before the Lord, but the Lord was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake came a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. After the fire came the sound of a gentle breeze, and there was the Lord.
When Elijah heard, he covered his face with his sheepskin cloak, went out, and stood beneath the cave. Behold, a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

Elijah said, “I have been most zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the children of Israel have forsaken Thy covenant. They have pulled down Thine altars and killed Thy prophets with the sword. I remain utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.”
The Lord said to him, “Go, return on your way, and you will come to the wilderness road of Damascus. Anoint Hazael as king of Syria.
Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel-meholah, as prophet in your place.
Whoever is spared from Hazael’s sword, Jehu will put to death; whoever is spared from Jehu’s sword, Elisha will put to death.
You will leave seven thousand men in Israel: every knee that has not bent the knee to Baal, and every mouth that has not bowed down to him.”

He sent to him a commander, a captain of fifty, with his fifty men. He went up and came to him, and there Elijah was, sitting on the top of the mountain. The captain of fifty spoke to him and said, ‘Man of God, the king has summoned you. Come down!’

Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, ‘If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.’ Fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
The king again sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty men. The captain went up and spoke to him, saying, ‘Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly!’
Elijah answered and spoke to him, saying, ‘If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.’ Fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

The king again sent a commander, a third captain of fifty, with his fifty men. The third captain of fifty came to him, bent his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty slaves of yours be honored in your eyes.’
‘Behold, fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains of fifty and their fifty men. But now please let the lives of your slaves be honored in your eyes.’
An angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said, ‘Go down with him; do not be afraid of them.’ Elijah rose and went down with him to the king.

Elijah spoke to him and said, ‘Thus says the Lord: Why did you send messengers to inquire of Baal Fly, the god of Ekron? It shall not be so! The bed onto which you have gone up—you will not come down from it, for you will surely die.’
He died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken.
When the Lord was about to take Elijah up in a tumult, as into heaven, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha, ‘Please stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel.’ Elisha said, ‘As the Lord lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.’ So they came to Bethel.
The sons of the prophets who were in Bethel came to Elisha and said to him, ‘Do you know that this day the Lord is taking your master away from above your head?’ He said, ‘I too know it. Be silent.’
Elijah said to Elisha, ‘Please stay here, for the Lord has sent me to Jericho.’ Elisha said, ‘As the Lord lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.’ So they came to Jericho.

The sons of the prophets who were in Jericho approached Elisha and said to him, ‘Do you know that this day the Lord is taking your master away from above your head?’ He said, ‘Indeed, I too know it. Be silent.’
Elijah said to him, ‘Please stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan.’ Elisha said, ‘As the Lord lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.’ So both of them went on.
Fifty men, sons of the prophets, stood opposite them at a distance, while both of them stood beside the Jordan.
Elijah took his sheepskin, rolled it up, and struck the water. The water divided to this side and that, and both of them crossed over on barren ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, ‘Ask what I should do for you before I am taken up from you.’ Elisha said, ‘Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.’
Elijah said, ‘You have made a difficult request. If you see me being taken up from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it certainly will not happen.’
As they went, walking and speaking, behold—a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah was taken up in a tumult, as into heaven.
Elisha was watching and crying, ‘Father, father! Israel’s chariot and its horseman!’ He saw him no more. He seized his clothes and tore them into two pieces.
He picked up Elijah’s sheepskin, which had fallen upon Elisha, and Elisha returned and stood on the edge of the Jordan.

He took Elijah’s sheepskin, which had fallen upon him, and struck the water, but it did not separate. He said, ‘Where is the God of Elijah—Appho?’ He struck the waters, and they split to this side and that, and Elisha crossed over.
The sons of the prophets in Jericho saw him from opposite him and said, ‘The spirit of Elijah has come to rest upon Elisha.’ They came to meet him and bowed before him to the ground.
Elisha died, and they buried him. Moab’s lightly equipped raiders came into the land when the year came round.
As they were burying the man, suddenly they saw the lightly equipped raider. They threw the man into Elisha’s grave. He went and touched Elisha’s bones, came to life, and stood on his feet.
Elijah was a human being with experiences like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months.
And he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
But in truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in Elijah’s days, when heaven was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was sent to none of them except to a widow at Zarephath in Sidon’s territory.
“And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,
who will restore a father’s heart toward a son and a person’s heart toward his neighbor, lest I come and strike the land utterly.”
“All of you, remember the law of Moses My servant, as I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel, ordinances and judgments.”
He will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

He himself will go before Him in Elijah’s spirit and power, to turn fathers’ hearts toward children and the disobedient to the understanding of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.”
The disciples asked Him, “Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He answered, “Elijah indeed comes and will restore all things.
But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. In the same way the Son of Man is also to suffer at their hands.”
Then the disciples understood that He spoke to them about John the Baptist.
Let the prophet in whom there is a dream tell his dream, and the one to whom My word comes tell My word in truth. What has chaff to do with wheat? So are My words, says the Lord.
Are not My words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting rock?
Moab broke faith with Israel after Ahab died.

Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and became ill. He sent messengers and said to them, ‘Come, and inquire of Baal Fly, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this illness of mine.’ And they went to inquire through him.

An angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘Rise, come to meet the messengers of Ahaziah king of Samaria, and say to them: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal Fly, the god of Ekron?’
‘It shall not be so! For thus says the Lord: The bed onto which you have gone up—you will not come down from it, for there you will surely die.’ And Elijah went and spoke to them.
The messengers returned to him, and he said to them, ‘Why have you returned?’

They said to him, ‘A man came up to meet us and said to us: Come, return to the king who sent you and tell him, Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal Fly, the god of Ekron? It shall not be so! The bed onto which you have gone up—you will not come down from it, for you will surely die.’
He spoke to them, saying, ‘What was the character of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?’
They said to him, ‘A hairy man, with a leather belt fastened around his waist.’ He said, ‘This is Elijah the Tishbite.’
The young attendants of the district rulers went out first. They sent out and reported to the king of Syria, “Men have come out of Samaria.”
He said to them, “If these men are coming out for peace, take them alive; if for war, take them alive.
And do not let the young attendants of the district rulers come out of the city.” The force behind them
struck, each man the one beside him, and each repeated the blow against the one beside him. Syria fled, and Israel pursued them. The son of Ader, king of Syria, escaped on a cavalryman’s horse.
The king of Israel went out, captured all the horses and chariots, and inflicted a great defeat on Syria.

The prophet approached the king of Israel and said, “Strengthen yourself. Understand and consider what you must do, for at the return of the year the son of Ader, king of Syria, is coming up against you.”

The attendants of the king of Syria said, “Israel’s God is a God of mountains and not a God of valleys; that is why He was stronger than we. But if we fight them on level ground, surely we will be stronger than they.
Do this: dismiss the kings, each to his own place, and appoint satraps in their place.
The king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went on. They made a circuit of seven days’ journey, but there was no water for the camp or the livestock at their feet.
The king of Israel said, ‘Alas! The Lord has called the three kings who are passing through to give them into the hand of Moab.’

Jehoshaphat said, ‘Is there no prophet of the Lord here, through whom we may inquire of the Lord?’ One of the attendants of the king of Israel answered, ‘Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on Elijah’s hands.’
Jehoshaphat said, ‘A word of the Lord is with him.’ The king of Israel, Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, ‘What have I to do with you? Go to your father’s prophets.’ The king of Israel said to him, ‘No! For the Lord has called the three kings together to hand them over into the hands of Moab.’
Elisha said, ‘As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if I were not showing regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would neither look toward you nor see you.’
‘But now bring me a player of strings.’ As the player plucked the strings, the hand of the Lord came upon him.
Elisha entered the house, and there was the child, dead, lying on his bed.
Elisha entered the house, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the Lord.
He went up and lay upon the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He bent over him, and the child’s flesh was warmed.
He returned and walked in the house this way and that. He went up and bent over the child as many as seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Elisha called out to Gehazi and said, ‘Call this Shunammite woman.’ He called, and she came in to him. Elisha said, ‘Take your son.’
The woman came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. She took her son and went out.

And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.

And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abou daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes, in accordance with everything his father David had done.

The rest of Hezekiah’s deeds, all his might, and what he made—the fountain and aqueduct—and how he brought water into the city—are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had arrived and that his face was set to wage war against Jerusalem.
He consulted with his elders and mighty men about blocking the waters of the springs outside the city, and they joined in strengthening him.
He gathered a great crowd and blocked the waters of the springs and the river that divided the city, saying, “Let the king of Assyria not come and find abundant water and gain strength.”
Hezekiah grew strong and built the entire demolished wall and towers, and outside another defensive wall. He strengthened the retaining work of the City of David and prepared many weapons.
King Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about these things and cried out to heaven.

The Lord sent an angel, and he wiped out every mighty warrior, ruler, and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. The king returned to his land with shame of face. He entered the house of his god, and some who had come from his own body struck him down with the sword.
The Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from everyone’s hand, and He gave them rest all around.
Hezekiah himself blocked the upper outlet of the water of Gihon and directed the waters downward toward the southwest of the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.
In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians went up against Judah’s fortified cities and captured them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish: ‘I have sinned. Withdraw from me; whatever you impose on me, I will bear.’ The king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the Lord’s house and in the treasuries of the king’s house.
At that time Hezekiah cut apart the doors of the Lord’s sanctuary and the fixed supports which Hezekiah king of Judah had gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.

The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.
When King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and entered the Lord’s house.
He sent Eliakim the steward, Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests, clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amos.
They said to him, ‘Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of affliction, rebuke, and provocation. Children have reached the birth pains, but the woman giving birth has no strength.

Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all Rhapsakes’s words, whom his master the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with words which the Lord your God has heard. Take up a prayer for the remnant that remains.’
King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, ‘Tell your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not fear the words you have heard, with which the king of the Assyrians’ young servants blasphemed.
Behold, I am putting a spirit within him. He shall hear a report and return to his land, and I shall bring him down by the sword in his land.’
Hezekiah took the letters from the messengers’ hand and read them. He went up to the Lord’s house, and Hezekiah unfolded them before the Lord.
He said, ‘Lord, Israel’s God, seated upon the cherubim, Thou alone art God among all the kingdoms of the earth. Thou madest heaven and earth.
Incline Thine ear, Lord, and hear. Open Thine eyes, Lord, and see. Hear Sennacherib’s words, which he sent to reproach the living God.
For truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have devastated the nations
and put their gods into the fire, for they are not gods but the work of human hands, wood and stones; so they destroyed them.
Now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth will know that Thou art the Lord, God alone.’
Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, Israel’s God: What you did pray to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.
By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.
Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed, went away, returned, and lived in Nineveh.
As he was bowing down in the house of Neserach his god, his sons Adramelech and Sarasar struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Asordan became king in his place.

In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. Isaiah son of Amos the prophet came to him and said, ‘Thus says the Lord: Give instructions for your house, for you are dying and shall not live.’
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,
‘I pray Thee, Lord, remember how I walked before Thee in truth and with a full heart, and did what was good in Thine eyes.’ Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Isaiah was in the middle courtyard when the Lord’s word came to him:

‘Return and tell Hezekiah, leader of My people: Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Behold, I shall heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the Lord’s house,
and I shall add fifteen years to your days. I shall save you and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’
He said, ‘Let them take a cake of figs and place it on the ulcer, and he will recover.’
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, ‘What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I shall go up to the Lord’s house on the third day?’
Isaiah said, ‘This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word He has spoken: The shadow will advance ten steps, if it returns ten steps.’
Hezekiah said, ‘It is easy for the shadow to incline ten steps. No, let the shadow return ten steps backward.’
Isaiah the prophet cried to the Lord, and the shadow returned backward ten steps on the stairway.
But the angel said to him, “Do not fear, Zechariah, for your petition has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great before the Lord. He will certainly drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and celebrate in her, all who love her! Rejoice with joy, all who mourn over her,
so that you may nurse and be filled from her comforting breast, so that, nursing fully, you may delight in the entrance of her glory.
For thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I turn toward them like a river of peace, and like a flooding torrent the glory of nations. Their children will be lifted on shoulders and comforted on knees.
As if a mother were to comfort someone, so I too will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.’
The Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
“Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is in Naboth’s vineyard, because he has gone down there to take possession of it.

Say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because you did murder and did take possession, therefore thus says the Lord: In every place where swine and dogs licked Naboth’s blood, dogs will lick your blood there, and prostitutes will bathe in your blood.’”
Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” He said, “I have found you, because you have been sold in vain to do evil before the Lord, provoking Him.

Thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I am bringing calamities upon you. I will burn out what remains after you and destroy from Ahab every male who urinates against a wall, both confined and abandoned in Israel.
I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocations you have provoked and because you did cause Israel to sin.’”
To Jezebel the Lord spoke, saying, “The dogs will devour her at Jezreel’s outer wall.”
Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; anyone belonging to him who dies in the plain, the birds of the heavens will eat.
In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came up against Judea’s fortified cities and took them.
The king of the Assyrians sent Rapsakes from Lachis to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large force. He stood at the upper pool’s aqueduct, on the road of the fuller’s field.
Eliakim son of Chelkias, the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joach son of Asaph, the record-keeper, went out to him.
Rapsakes said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: ‘What do you trust in?
When King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments, wrapped himself in sackcloth, and went up to the Lord’s house.
He sent Eliakim the steward, Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests, wrapped in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amos.
They said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah: Today is a day of distress, reproach, reproof, and wrath, for labor has come upon the woman giving birth, but she has no strength to give birth.

May the Lord your God hear Rapsakes’ words, which the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to reproach words that the Lord your God has heard. You shall plead with the Lord your God for those who remain.”
The king’s servants came to Isaiah,
and Isaiah said to them, “You shall say this to your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not fear the words you heard, with which the king of the Assyrians’ envoys reproached Me.
Behold, I will put a spirit into him. On hearing a report he will return to his country, and he will fall by the sword in his own land.”
Isaiah son of Amos was sent to Hezekiah and said to him, “Thus says the Lord, God of Israel: I heard what you prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of the Assyrians.
This is the word God spoke concerning him: Virgin daughter Zion despised and sneered at you; daughter Jerusalem shook her head over you.
Whom did you reproach and provoke? Against whom did you raise your voice? Yet you did not lift your eyes on high toward the Holy One of Israel.

For through messengers you reproached the Lord. You said, ‘With my many chariots I climbed the mountain heights and the furthest reaches of Lebanon. I cut down its cedar’s height and the cypress’s beauty, and entered the height of a part of the woodland.
An angel of the Lord went out and killed one hundred eighty-five thousand from the Assyrians’ camp. On rising early in the morning, they found all the bodies dead.

At that time Hezekiah became ill to the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amos came to him and said, “Thus says the Lord: Arrange your household’s affairs, for you are dying and will not live.”
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the Lord,
saying, “Remember, Lord, how I walked before Thee with truth, in a true heart, and did what was pleasing before Thee.” Hezekiah wept greatly.
The Lord’s word came to Isaiah, saying,
“Go and tell Hezekiah: Thus says the Lord, God of David your father: I heard the voice of your prayer and saw your tears. Behold, I am adding fifteen years to your time.
I will save you from the king of the Assyrians’ hand, and I will shield this city.
This is your sign from the Lord that God will do this thing:”
“As for the shadow of the steps the sun descended—the ten steps of your father’s house—I will turn the sun back ten steps.” The sun went up the ten steps which the shadow had descended.
Comfort, comfort My people, says God.
You priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her. For her humiliation is fulfilled, her sin is loosed; for from the hand of the Lord she has received double for her sins.
The Lord’s spirit is upon me, because He anointed me. He sent me to bring good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind,
to announce the Lord’s acceptable year and a day of recompense, to comfort all who mourn,

so that Zion’s mourners may receive glory instead of ashes, an ointment of joy for those who mourn, a robe of glory instead of a spirit of despondency. They will be called Generations of Righteousness, the Lord’s planting, for glory.
Thus says the Lord God, who made heaven and fixed it in place, established the earth and its contents, and gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those treading it:
“I, the Lord God, called you in righteousness; I will hold your hand and strengthen you. I gave you as a covenant for a people, a light for nations,
to open blind people’s eyes, bring those bound out of bonds, and those sitting in darkness out of the prison house.
I am the Lord God; this is My name. I will not give My glory to another or My praiseworthy deeds to carved images.
Behold, the things from the beginning have arrived, and new things I will announce; before they spring up, they were disclosed to you.”
Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jedida daughter of Edeia, from Basouroth.
He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes and walked in every way of his father David, turning aside neither right nor left.
The king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king went up to the Lord’s house, with every man of Judah and all who inhabited Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the covenant book found in the Lord’s house.

The king stood beside the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord: to follow the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and whole soul, upholding the words of this covenant, the things written in this book. All the people stood in the covenant.

The king commanded Chelkias the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the doorpost guards to bring out of the Lord’s sanctuary all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all heaven’s host. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the sademoth of Kidron and took their dust to Bethel.

He put an end to the chomarim whom Judah’s kings had appointed, who burned incense at the high places and in Judah’s cities and the places around Jerusalem, and to those burning incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, the mazouroth, and all heaven’s host.

He brought the grove out of the Lord’s house, outside Jerusalem to the Kidron torrent. He burned it in the Kidron torrent, reduced it to dust, and threw its dust into the grave of the sons of the people.
Before him there was no king like him who returned to the Lord with his whole heart, his whole soul, and all his strength, according to all Moses’ law; and after him none like him arose.
In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, Nabouzardan, the chief cook who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He set fire to the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all Jerusalem’s houses; every house was set ablaze by
the chief cook.
Nabouzardan, the chief cook, removed the rest of the people left in the city, those who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the remaining support.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
Before I formed you in the belly, I know you; before you came out of the womb, I have consecrated you. I have appointed you a prophet to nations.
I said, O Master Lord! Behold, I do not know how to speak, because I am young.
The Lord said to me, Do not say, I am young, because you will go to everyone to whom I send you, and you will speak according to everything I command you.
Do not fear them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.
The Lord stretched out His hand toward me and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, Behold, I have put My words into your mouth.
Behold, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant.

and I looked, and behold, a sweeping wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud was within it, with brightness around it and fire flashing like lightning; within it was something like the appearance of electrum, within the fire, and brightness within it.

and each had four faces, and each had four wings.
Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.

I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.

Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the arrangement of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord’s glory. I saw it, and I fall upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.
The cherubim lifted themselves. This was the living creature I had seen at the river Chebar.
When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them. When the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, their wheels did not turn.
When they stood, these stood; when they rose, these rose with them, because a spirit of life was in them.
The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.
I will judge him with death, blood, flooding rain and hailstones. I will rain fire and sulfur upon him, all those with him and the many nations with him.
I will be magnified, sanctified, glorified and made known before many nations, and they will know that I am the Lord.’”
On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will take you, Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, My servant, says the Lord, and make you like a signet, for I have chosen you, says the Lord Almighty.”
A name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

In the eighth year of his reign, while still a boy, he began to seek the Lord, the God of his father David. In the twelfth year of his reign he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, sacred groves, and cast objects.

He pulled down before him the altars of the Baals and the high places upon them. He cut down the sacred groves, shattered and pulverized the carved and cast objects, and scattered them over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He burned priests’ bones upon the altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the cities of Ephraim, Manasseh, Simeon, and Naphtali, and in their surrounding places,
he pulled down the sacred groves and altars, cut the idols into fine pieces, and cut down all the high places throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

The king stood by the pillar and established a covenant before the Lord: to walk before the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and the whole soul—the words of the covenant written in this book.
He made everyone found in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand. The inhabitants of Jerusalem made a covenant in the house of the Lord, the God of their fathers.

Josiah removed all the abominations from all the land belonging to the sons of Israel and made everyone present in Jerusalem and Israel serve the Lord their God throughout his days. He did not turn aside from following the Lord, the God of his fathers.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did what was evil before the Lord his God. He felt no shame before Jeremiah the prophet, and at what came from the Lord’s mouth,
in breaking his obligations to King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He hardened his neck and strengthened his heart so as not to return to the Lord God of Israel.
All the distinguished men of Judah, the priests, and the people of the land multiplied breaches of faith in the nations’ abominations and defiled the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.
The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

He brought against them a king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Zedekiah. They had no mercy on their virgins and carried away their elders. He handed everything into their hands.
All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and the magnates—he brought everything into Babylon.
He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.
He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
The Lord Almighty answered the angel speaking within me with good words and comforting speeches.
The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy,
and I am angry with great anger at the nations joining in assault, because I was a little angry, but they joined in attacking to bring evils.
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in compassion, and My house will be rebuilt in her, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure will again be extended over Jerusalem.”
The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Cities will again overflow with good things; the Lord will again have mercy on Zion and again choose Jerusalem.”

Iesous son of Iosedek and his brothers the priests, and Zorobabel son of Salathiel and his brothers, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer whole burnt offerings upon it according to what is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
Haggai the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo prophesied a prophecy over the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, over them.
Then Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesous son of Iosedek arose and began building the house of God in Jerusalem. God’s prophets were with them, helping them.
The wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Eloul, in fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard, all the nations around us became afraid. Great fear fell upon them before their eyes, and they knew that it was by our God that this work had been brought to completion.
When the wall had been built, I set up the doors, and the gatekeepers, singers and Levites were appointed.
I gave orders to my brother Anania and to Anania, ruler of the bira in Jerusalem, for he was a truthful man and feared God more than many,

and I said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until the sun is up. While they are still keeping watch, let the doors be closed and wedged fast. Appoint advance guards from those living in Jerusalem, each at his guard post and each opposite his house.”
The city was broad and large, but the people in it were few, and no houses had been built.
And Enoch lived one hundred and sixty-five years, and begot Methuselah.
And Enoch pleased God for two hundred years after he begot Methuselah, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
And Enoch pleased God, and was not found, for God transferred him.
By faith Enoch was taken away so as not to see death, and he was not found, because God took him away. For before his taking away he had received testimony that he had pleased God.
And Joseph spoke to his brothers, saying, “I am dying; but God shall surely visit you, and bring you up from this land to the land which God swore to our fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.”
And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “In the visitation with which God shall visit you, you shall carry up my bones from here with you.”
And Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old; and they performed his burial rites, and laid him in a coffin in Egypt.
Moses took Joseph’s bones with him, for Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, “The Lord will surely visit you, and you shall carry my bones up from here with you.”

The sons of Israel brought Joseph’s bones up from Egypt and buried them at Shechem in the portion of the field that Jacob acquired from the Amorites living at Shechem for one hundred ewe lambs; he gave it to Joseph as a portion.
This is the book of the generations of mankind. On the day when God made Adam, He made him in the image of God.
Male and female He made them, and He blessed them, and named them Adam on the day when He made them.
And Adam lived two hundred and thirty years, and begot a son in his own likeness and image, and named him Seth.
And he said: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.
May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the houses of Shem; and let Canaan be their servant.

And God said, “Let Us make man in Our image and likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God made man; in the image of God He made him; male and female He made them.

And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, all the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face firmly against Gog and the land of Magog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel, and prophesy against him,
and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,
and I will gather you and all your force, horses and horsemen all clothed in breastplates, a great assembly, small shields, helmets and swords,
Persians, Ethiopians and Libyans, all with helmets and small shields;
Gomer and all those around him, the house of Thergama from the farthest north and all those around him, and many nations with you.
Be made ready; prepare yourself, you and all your assembly gathered with you, and you will be a guard for Me.

After many days he will be prepared, and at the end of years he will come and reach the land turned back from the sword, of those gathered from many nations, upon Israel’s land that had been wholly desolate. This one has come out of nations, and all will dwell in peace.
You will come up like rain and arrive like a cloud to cover the land; you will be there, with all those around you and many nations with you.
You shall make a holy robe for Aaron your brother, for honour and glory.
Speak to everyone skilled in understanding whom I have filled with a spirit of perception. They shall make Aaron’s holy robe for the sanctuary, in which he shall serve Me as priest.

These are the robes they shall make: a breastpiece, a shoulder-piece, a full-length robe, a tasselled tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy robes for Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.

Around the under-robe’s lower hem you shall make little pomegranates like those of a flowering pomegranate tree, of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen; likewise gold pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
Beside a gold pomegranate there shall be a bell and a floral ornament around the under-robe’s hem.
And Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers, as he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord and as he goes out, so that he does not die.
And Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be an everlasting statute for you throughout your generations.

But if you go out to war in your land against the adversaries who resist you, you shall give a signal with the trumpets; and you shall be remembered before the Lord, and shall be delivered from your enemies.

And in the days of your gladness, and at your feasts, and at your new moons, you shall blow the trumpets over your whole burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of deliverance; and it shall be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.
And Aaron lifted his hands over the people and blessed them. He came down after preparing the offering for sin, the whole burnt offerings, and the deliverance offerings.
And Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Testimony. They came out and blessed all the people, and the Lord’s glory appeared to all the people.
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed what was on the altar, both the whole burnt offerings and the fat. All the people saw, were astonished, and fell on their faces.

And the Lord said unto Moses: Speak unto Aaron your brother, and let him not enter at all times into the holy place within the veil, before the propitiatory cover which is upon the ark of testimony, so that he does not die; for I will appear in a cloud above the propitiatory cover.
In this way Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a calf from the cattle for sin and a ram for a whole burnt offering.

And he shall put on a consecrated linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his skin, gird himself with a linen belt, and put on a linen turban. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.
And he shall take the firepan full of burning coals from the altar opposite the Lord, fill his hands with finely compounded incense, and bring them within the veil,
and put the incense on the fire before the Lord. The vapour of incense shall cover the propitiatory cover above the testimonies, and he shall not die.

And he shall take some of the calf’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the propitiatory cover toward the east; before the propitiatory cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

And he shall slaughter the male young goat for the people’s sin offering before the Lord and bring some of its blood within the veil. He shall do with its blood as he did with the calf’s blood, sprinkling its blood on the propitiatory cover, before the propitiatory cover,

and make atonement for the holy place from the sons of Israel’s uncleannesses and their wrongdoings, concerning all their sins. He shall do the same for the Tent of Testimony established among them amid their uncleanness.

And no one shall be in the Tent of Testimony when he enters to make atonement in the holy place until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself, his house, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.

My dove, my perfect one, is the only one; she is the only one of her mother, the chosen one of the woman who bore her. Daughters saw her and will call her blessed; queens and concubines will praise her.
Who is this looking out like dawn, beautiful like the moon, chosen like the sun, a terror like troops drawn up?
I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit; his fragrance will be like Lebanon.
They will return and settle beneath his shelter; they will live and be filled to intoxication with grain. His memorial will blossom like a vine, like Lebanon’s wine.
I rose high like a cedar in Lebanon, like a cypress in the mountains of Hermon.
I rose high like a palm in En-gedi, like rose plants in Jericho, like a stately olive in the plain; I rose high like a plane tree.
A righteous person will blossom like a palm tree; like the cedar in Lebanon he will multiply.
Planted in the Lord’s house, they will blossom in the courts of our God.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.
And speak unto the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male young goat from the goats for sin, and a calf and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a whole offering,
and a calf and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.
And they brought what Moses commanded opposite the Tent of Testimony, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the Lord.
And Moses said: Do this thing which the Lord said, and the glory of the Lord shall appear among you.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Draw near unto the altar, and prepare your offering for sin and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your house; and prepare the gifts of the people, and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Aaron drew near unto the altar and slaughtered the calf for the sin offering.
And Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood, put it on the altar’s horns, and poured the blood at the altar’s base.
And its drink offering shall be a fourth of a hin for each lamb; in the holy place you shall pour out a drink offering of strong drink unto the Lord.
butter of cattle and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, young bulls and goats, with the fat of the kernels of wheat; and they drank wine, the blood of the grape.

Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be offered on the altar. When they began offering the burnt offering, they began singing to the Lord, and the trumpets accompanied the instruments of David king of Israel.
The whole assembly worshiped, the psalm singers sang, and the trumpets sounded until the burnt offering was finished.
When they finished offering, the king and everyone present bent down and worshiped.
King Hezekiah and the rulers told the Levites to hymn the Lord with the words of David and Asaph the prophet. They hymned with rejoicing, fell down, and worshiped.

and all the Levitical singers belonging to the sons of Asaph, to Heman, and to Idithoun, and their sons and their brethren, clothed in fine-linen robes, with cymbals, nablai, and kinyrai, stood opposite the altar, and with them were a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets,

there was one voice in trumpeting, singing psalms, and shouting, to give thanks and praise to the Lord. When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, and the Lord’s glory filled the house.

All Israel’s sons saw the fire descending and the Lord’s glory upon the house. They fell face down to the earth upon the stone pavement, worshiped, and praised the Lord: “For it is good, for His mercy endures for ever.”
Esdras the priest brought the law before the assembly—men, women and everyone able to understand by listening—on the first day of the seventh month,
and read from it from the hour when the sun gave light until midday, before the men and women, who were understanding; the ears of all the people were directed toward the book of the law.

Esdras the scribe stood on a wooden platform. Beside him stood Mattathias, Samaias, Ananias, Ouria, Elkia and Maasaia on his right, and on his left Phadaias, Misael, Melchias, Osam, Asabdana, Zacharias and Mosollam.
Esdras opened the book before all the people—for he was above the people—and when he opened it, all the people stood.
Esdras blessed the Lord, the great God. All the people answered and said, “Amen,” lifting their hands, and they bowed and worshiped the Lord with their faces to the ground.
For Thou art my endurance, Lord; the Lord is my hope from my youth.
Upon Thee I was supported from the womb; from my mother’s belly Thou art the One who shelters me. My hymn is continually in Thee.
And may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
Ask, then, for the things that bring Jerusalem peace, and prosperity for those who love you.
May there be peace within your strength, and prosperity within your fortified towers.
For the sake of my brothers and neighbors, I was speaking peace concerning you.
I will set this in my heart; therefore I will endure.
The Lord is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that will seek Him as good
and will endure and be quiet for the Lord’s salvation.
Fourteen: Noun. Thy word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths.
The disclosure of Thy words will give light and understanding to the simple.
Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my utterance be awaited as the rain, and let my words descend as the dew, as a shower upon the grass, and as snow upon the herbage.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness unto our God.
For with the Lord is mercy, and with Him is abundant redemption,
And He will redeem Israel from all its lawless deeds.
Thirteen: Mēm. How I loved Thy law, Lord! It is my meditation all day.
Thou madest me wiser than my enemies in Thy commandment, for it is mine for ever.
